questions.title: What should you do if your ball is hidden under sand in a bunker?
questions.question: You hit your ball into a bunker and now it is covered by sand so you can't see it. What are you allowed to do to find your ball?

choices.text: You can use your club or feet to look for the ball. If the ball moves, you have to put it back and fix the sand like it was.
Leave the hidden ball and play with a new ball.
Dig up the ball and just hit it from wherever it ends up in the sand.
Ask someone else to find your ball, but you are not allowed to touch the sand.

questions.explanation: If your ball is hidden under sand in a bunker, you can gently use your club or feet to find it. If the ball moves, you must put it back where it was and make the sand look the same as before.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A place on the golf course full of sand, also called a sand trap.
How the ball is sitting on the ground, like on top or under the sand.

questions.teachingTip: Let children try finding a buried ball in the sand and practice putting it back as it was.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think they can just dig out the ball and hit it right away.
Some may think they must play a new ball if their ball is hidden.
They might not know they can touch the sand to look for the ball.

questions.title: What can you do if your ball sinks into the bunker?
questions.question: After your shot, you can't see your ball because it's buried under the sand in a bunker. What are you allowed to do to find it?

choices.text: Use your club or feet to search for it; if the ball moves, you must replace it and recreate the lie
Leave it hidden and play a different ball
Dig out the ball and just play it from where it ends up
Ask someone else to find your ball, but you can't move any sand

questions.explanation: You can carefully use your club or feet to find your buried ball. If you move it while searching, you must put it back where it was and recreate the original lie without penalty.
